summary: The new Section 4.3 integration is not runnable because the PowerShell driver contains a form-feed character where the path separator should be. The expanded input set also lacks an updated checksum manifest, so the newly incorporated tables cannot yet be tied to frozen inputs.

findings.title: The driver calls a nonexistent path after completing the two-hour Stata run
findings.what_the_code_does: The command is `python (Join-Path $repo "MATCHING\fs_draft_tables.py") $paper`, but the character displayed between `MATCHING` and `s_draft_tables.py` is byte `0x0C` (form feed), not a slash followed by `f`. PowerShell therefore constructs an illegal/nonexistent path rather than `MATCHING/fs_draft_tables.py`.
findings.why_it_matters: Every Machine A reproduction now fails immediately after the lengthy Stata stage. The Section 4.3 draft tables and subsequent claim check are never run, so the advertised one-command reproduction is broken.
findings.how_to_check: Run `Format-Hex replication/Run-MachineA.ps1` and inspect offset `0x09F0`, which contains `... MATCHING 0C 73 ...`. Then compare `Test-Path (Join-Path (Resolve-Path .) 'MATCHING\fs_draft_tables.py')` with the path constructed from the current line.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the form-feed character with a normal path separator so the argument is exactly `MATCHING\fs_draft_tables.py`, then run the driver through the Python step.

findings.title: The 285 newly required inputs have no recorded checksums
findings.what_the_code_does: `input_list()` now adds three FamilySearch link files and every matching `norace*.dta`, while the tracked manifest still declares only 104 files and 103 frozen inputs from 2026-11-01. Consequently, `hash_inputs.py --check` treats all 285 additions as new and fails rather than verifying them against frozen hashes.
findings.why_it_matters: Tables 9–11 depend on inputs whose identity is not captured by the replication archive. The README calls these frozen inputs, but neither an author nor a replicator can verify that the files used for the committed Section 4.3 results are the same files currently present.
findings.how_to_check: Run `rg -n "link1930_1940_fs|divided_file1930_ans|divided_file1940_ans" replication/input_manifest.md`; it returns no rows. On Machine A, `python replication/hash_inputs.py --check` should report the 285 files as changed or new.
findings.suggested_fix: On Machine A, regenerate `replication/input_manifest.md` with the expanded input list after confirming these are the exact files used for the committed results, review the hashes and counts, and commit the updated manifest.

findings.title: Checksum verification does not detect a divided-file shard removed from disk
findings.what_the_code_does: The current file list is built dynamically with `d.glob("norace*.dta")`, and check mode only tests `old.get(short(f)) != digest` for files still in that current list. It never computes manifest paths absent from the current list, so removal of one shard is omitted from verification and can still yield exit status 0.
findings.why_it_matters: A partial divided-file collection can be reported unchanged after the manifest is regenerated. The Stata scripts likewise enumerate the surviving shards, so a missing state/partition is not rejected at preflight and can alter the fixed-initial rows used in Tables 9–11.
findings.how_to_check: On Machine A, run `python -c "import replication.hash_inputs as h; old=set(h.read_manifest()); cur={h.short(f) for f in h.input_list()}; print(sorted(old-cur))"`. After temporarily making one manifested shard unavailable, the command identifies it, whereas the present `--check` loop has no equivalent test.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare the full set of manifest paths with the current input set and fail on both `old-current` and `current-old`. Also assert the expected shard count per year, or store the authoritative shard list rather than accepting any nonempty glob.

verified_clean.item: The added Stata preflight includes all three FamilySearch link variants and both divided-file directories.
verified_clean.evidence: The link files are appended at replication/run_machineA.do:52-54 and both years of divided files at replication/run_machineA.do:55-61.

verified_clean.item: Missing numeric ages are explicitly excluded from the Section 4.3 sample.
verified_clean.evidence: Both scripts use `age>=10 & age<.`, avoiding Stata's positive-infinity missing-value trap: MATCHING/fs_avg_performance.do:74-76 and MATCHING/fs_cells.do:119-121.

verified_clean.item: The model-agreement cells exclude empty model fields and assert that the four principal cells partition human-complete discordant records.
verified_clean.evidence: MATCHING/fs_cells.do:73-81 constructs `disc`, requires both model fields for `ml_ok`, and asserts cells 1–4 for every `disc` observation.

verified_clean.item: The new Section 4.3 scripts gate their principal Ancestry and ML results against the existing Table 4 counts and rates before writing output.
verified_clean.evidence: MATCHING/fs_avg_performance.do:100-153 and MATCHING/fs_cells.do:141-162 stop with exit code 9 when the target sample or benchmark columns do not reproduce.

verified_clean.item: The new Python files parse successfully, and the table formatter asserts expected rows, panel order, and the target total.
verified_clean.evidence: Static `ast.parse` succeeded for replication/hash_inputs.py and MATCHING/fs_draft_tables.py; structural assertions appear at MATCHING/fs_draft_tables.py:57-59, MATCHING/fs_draft_tables.py:94, and MATCHING/fs_draft_tables.py:107.

verified_clean.item: The Section 4.3 generated exhibits are registered in the existing claim-check configuration.
verified_clean.evidence: replication/claims.toml:537-670 and replication/claims.toml:973-985 map the three figures files to the two Stata scripts and formatter.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied, so claims-vs-code language and reported interpretations could not be checked.
The external data were unavailable and the Stata pipeline was not run; dataset uniqueness, actual shard counts, merge outcomes, and reported numerical reproduction remain unverified.
Identification concerns about linkage selection and circular use of transcription sources could be traced in the code, but their treatment in the paper could not be assessed without the draft.
The review was limited to the uncommitted changes, the newly invoked Section 4.3 scripts, and directly related replication files; it was not a full-repository audit.
